definition.title: Write a blog post from notes, a PR or a draft
definition.description: Turn material you already have (meeting notes, a merged pull request, a draft or a record of work) into a guide for your site's readers: it finds the question your material answers, plans the post, drafts it, reviews and revises it, and checks the copy. The draft waits in Decisions with the claims to confirm; Tin never publishes it.

human_review.summary: Read the post and confirm the claims Tin lists before it goes on the site.

prerequisites.reason: The writing style guide gives the post the founder's voice.
The growth plan names the readers the post is written for.

seed_path.title: Seed file
seed_path.description: The material to write from, as a file in project Files: meeting notes, a merged pull request's description and diff summary, a draft or a record of work. Commit it first, for example as context/notes/<date>-<topic>.md with a source line at the top. Raw material works best: Tin plans the post itself.

seed_text.title: Or paste the material
seed_text.description: Material that has no file. With a seed file too, Tin reads both.

direction.title: Optional direction
direction.description: The angle, reader or point you want, in a sentence or two. Tin treats it as decided.

style_path.title: Optional writing guide
style_path.description: A writing guide in project Files to write in, such as one author's guide. Without it, Tin uses the project's writing style guide.

revise_path.title: Draft to revise
revise_path.description: To revise an earlier draft instead of writing a new one: its file under content/drafts. Needs feedback.

feedback.title: Feedback for the revision
feedback.description: What to change in the draft to revise. Tin applies all of it and keeps the rest.
